finding: A buffered write that fails at close leaves a partial settings file that the next start then skips as 'exists'.
why: A small file is only buffered by open(target, 'xb'), so a disk-full OSError is raised at the with-exit close, outside the inner try that unlinks the target; checked with io.BufferedWriter over a raw stream whose write raises: write() returned, close() raised.
fix: Unlink the target in the outer `except OSError` (when this call created it), or write to a temporary name and os.replace it.

finding: Possible duplicate agent name: the lowest-agent-id-wins check misses the interleaving where the higher id writes and reads first.
why: With a1 and a2 both holding the stale name N: a2 records N and reads (no a1 yet), a1 records N and reads (a2 > a1, so a1 keeps it); both end with N and both start. (also raised by delta-sweep and test-veracity)
fix: Check and claim the name inside the single manifest write (record_entry's change callback, under the lock), so the later writer always sees the earlier one and renames.
evidence: if not any(a["agent_id"] < agent_id and name in (a["pane_label"], a["agent_name"]) for a in again["agents"]): break  (the test only races a1 first: `a1's start wrote the same name first`)

finding: The new record lock guards add_owner only; adopt() in scripts/remove-worktree.py still rewrites the same record unlocked from an earlier read
why: A SessionStart prune that adopts a worktree can overwrite an owner add_owner just added, so the lost-owner race the lock closes stays open.
fix: Take the same lock in adopt() and re-read inside it, or move the locked read-modify-write into one worktree_owner function both call.
evidence: remove-worktree.py:416-418: known = owner.owners_of(record); record["owners"] = known + ...; record_file.write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8") (no lock; record read earlier by records())

finding: _record_lock retries a persistent OSError forever: the bare `except OSError: continue` skips both the LOCK_WAIT deadline and the sleep
why: If os.remove of a stale lock keeps failing (for example PermissionError), the loop spins with no timeout inside agent-start, past its 120 s budget (inferred from the code, not reproduced).
fix: Count the retry against the deadline: raise once time.monotonic() > end, and sleep before retrying any error other than a vanished lock.
evidence: try: if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(lock) > LOCK_STALE: os.remove(lock); continue / except OSError: continue / if time.monotonic() > end: raise ...

finding: When the 5th pass still finds a conflict, the renamed label and name are never recorded, yet the transport call uses them.
why: The loop ends right after the rename on its last pass, so the manifest keeps the conflicting name while the agent starts under a different one.
fix: Record after the last rename, or refuse with exit 4 naming the unresolved name when the 5 passes run out.
evidence: for _ in range(5): ... record_entry(...) ... label, name = _name(p.verb, run, again, ...)  (no break, no record after the last rename)

finding: A start-request `effort` that is a list or object raises TypeError and answers exit 4 'unavailable', not exit 2 naming the field.
why: `body["effort"] not in EFFORTS` hashes the value in a dict, and run_command's catch-all turns the TypeError into an unavailable answer.
fix: Check isinstance(body["effort"], str) first and refuse with contract.bad naming `effort`.
evidence: if body.get("effort") not in (None, "") and body["effort"] not in EFFORTS:  (EFFORTS is a dict, entry.py:45)

finding: The message-id form is not disjoint across senders when an agent id ends in -sup: agent `x-sup` sends `x-sup-1`, and the job supervisor of agent `x` sends `x-sup-1`
why: D-142 claims the form keeps every sender's ids disjoint, but both ids pass the check and share one inbox file name and one duplicate key.
fix: Refuse agent ids that end in -sup where the contact agent writes entries, or give the supervisor form a separator no agent id can hold.
evidence: re.fullmatch(rf"{re.escape(sender_id)}-(sup-)?[0-9]+", message_id); D-142: "B keeps every sender's ids disjoint"

finding: New helper refuse_the_write_after duplicates the inline lambda that test_exit_5_omits_pane_fields still carries 6 lines above
why: A near-copy left beside its twin drifts when the refusal rule changes.
fix: Use the helper in the earlier test too, or inline the one new use.
evidence: line 319 and line 328 both: lambda r, f, e: (_ for _ in ()).throw(manifest.ManifestBusy("x")) if "pid" in e else real(r, f, e)

finding: The gone-agent-close-fails test branches with if/else on the parameter and holds a vacuous clause
why: An if/else steering the asserts hides which kind is checked, and `"pane_id" not in body or kind == "multiplexer"` cannot fail for the multiplexer row.
fix: Split into a pane-kind test, a terminal-kind test and a no-pane-kind test, or put the expected state and fields in the parameters.
evidence: `if named: ... assert "pane_id" not in body or kind == "multiplexer" ... else: assert "pane_closed" not in body ...`

finding: The late-dialog watch is tested for a plain start only; the Codex resume path that herdr.md now says runs the same watch has no test
why: herdr.md:37 and herdr.py:149 apply the watch after a resume, but no test starts a resume where the status turns blocked inside the window.
fix: Add a case with resume='sess-7' on codex and a status list ending in blocked that expects exit 4 with dialog true.
evidence: herdr.md delta: "then `agent rename <pane> <name>`, then the same 3 s `agent get` watch as `agent-start`"; grep of 'resume' in test_team_transport.py shows lines 579 and 1087 only, neither sets a blocked status after the rename.

finding: The 'waits for the record lock' test never shows that add_owner waits
why: It asserts only that an OSError names the lock after LOCK_WAIT, so an implementation that fails at once with the same message passes; it also joins the time-out and stale-takeover behaviours in one body.
fix: Release the lock from a timer inside LOCK_WAIT and assert the write succeeds, and move the stale takeover to its own test.
evidence: `monkeypatch.setattr(owner, "LOCK_WAIT", 0.2) ... except OSError as busy: assert "lock" in str(busy)`

finding: The parallel add_owner test may pass without the lock (possible)
why: 8 processes race over a read-change-write window of a few milliseconds, so a lost update is rare and the test is a weak detector of a missing lock.
fix: Rely on the deterministic lock test, or make the race certain (a child holds the lock while the others start) so the test fails without the lock.
evidence: `children = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code, str(n)]) for n in range(100, 108)]` with no barrier; the git calls in add_owner run before the record is read, so the unlocked window is the read-to-os.replace span. Inferred, not run.

finding: Possible double hold of the record lock when two waiters take over the same stale lock.
why: Waiter 2 passes the age test, waiter 1 removes the stale lock and creates a fresh one, then waiter 2 removes waiter 1's fresh lock and creates its own, so both write the record. (also raised by delta-sweep)
fix: Take over by os.replace of a uniquely named file, or re-check the lock's age/identity right before os.remove.
